requirements.summary: Project badges must roll up to highest-severity active attention while the attention center preserves per-item precision.
requirements.raw_excerpt:
Recommended rollup rule:
  - project badge/card shows highest-severity active item plus count
  - attention center shows each active item separately
  - rows remain object-linked; they do not collapse into one synthetic project blocked blob

requirements.summary: Quiet and suppression controls must not remove canonical blocked or approval-wait attention rows.
requirements.raw_excerpt: quiet or temporary suppression should only affect resurfacing of advisory items, not erase canonical blocked or approval-wait rows

requirements.summary: Required concrete-account requests must not degrade silently and should become blocked or explicit override failure if unmet.
requirements.raw_excerpt: required concrete-account requests should not silently degrade into ordinary switching behavior

requirements.summary: Attention-center normalization must define a shared project-attention item contract and route rows to owning objects with explicit trust qualification.
requirements.raw_excerpt: Shared project-attention contract is missing; rows should reference canonical owners, carry next action routing, and disclose projection-derived trust.

requirements.summary: Attention item schema should include route payload, trust, dismissibility, quiet windows, active state, and lifecycle timestamps.
requirements.raw_excerpt: Recommended project_attention_item fields include route payload ref/inline, projection_trust_state, dismissibility_kind, quiet_until_utc, active, created_at_utc, updated_at_utc, and resolved_at_utc.

requirements.summary: Requested concrete-account modeling requires requested_account_id plus requested_account_binding values none, preferred, and required.
requirements.raw_excerpt: Recommended requested_account_binding values are none, preferred, required; requested_account_policy remains distinct from requested concrete account.

decisions.summary: Project storage should use dedicated projection families instead of overloading registry or UI-state records.
decisions.raw_excerpt: The cleaner model is a dedicated projection family with one current project_summary row per project and many project_attention_item rows per project.
decisions.decision_rationale: Preserves separation between registry identity, shell restore state, operational summary, and actionable attention objects.
rejected_alternatives: Store canonical attention truth in project_state:v1:{project_id}

decisions.summary: Routing should use one canonical internal payload and treat resume_url as transport serialization only.
decisions.raw_excerpt: Treat resume_url as a serialized transport form of route payload; URL deep links decode into the same route model used by in-app dispatch.
decisions.decision_rationale: Prevents fragmented navigation semantics across deep links, commands, palette, and attention surfaces.
rejected_alternatives: Maintain separate deep-link and in-app routing ontologies

decisions.summary: Runtime contracts should add durable actor-role projection and operational identity disclosure instead of reconstructing these per surface.
decisions.raw_excerpt: Identity and provider closure notes call for execution_role or actor_kind and operational_identity in canonical runtime, attempt, and usage records.
decisions.decision_rationale: Eliminates projection drift and improves requested/effective account auditability.
rejected_alternatives: Infer role and operational identity heuristically in each consumer surface

data_shapes.summary: A normalized project_attention_item contract is proposed with severity, owner, source, route payload, trust, and lifecycle fields.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: Recommended minimum shape includes attention_item_id, project_id, severity, owner_kind, reason_code, source_kind, source_object_ref, primary_route_payload, projection_trust_state, dismissibility_kind.

data_shapes.summary: A project_summary projection schema is proposed with activity, attention, health, counts, ownership, and freshness fields.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: Recommended project_summary fields include project_id, activity_state, attention_state, health_state, owner pointers, counts, projection_trust_state, and freshness timestamps.

data_shapes.summary: A canonical route payload field set is proposed for cross-surface navigation and restoration.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: Route payload fields include project_id, destination_surface, destination_tab, focused_run_id, historical_mode, thread_id, wizard_id, object refs, and inspector targets.

data_shapes.summary: Storage families should separate registry, UI restore state, operational summary, and per-item attention projections.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: projects:v1 is registry, project_state:v1:{project_id} is shell state, while operational summary and attention should live in dedicated projections.

data_shapes.summary: Requested account schema should include requested_account_id and requested_account_binding with none, preferred, and required semantics.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: requested_account_policy and requested_account_id solve different problems and requested_account_binding encodes hard vs soft request semantics.

routing_rules.summary: Attention routing must use the same internal payload model across in-app actions and URL/deep-link decoding.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: Project attention rows should route through the same payload model as deep links, search, and palette results.

routing_rules.summary: Attention and search routes must carry explicit target context and cannot rely on ambient UI state.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: Attention-center items should store inline route payload or a stable route reference rather than ambient state assumptions.

routing_rules.summary: Command-level navigation should resolve to canonical route payloads and avoid panel-centric shallow argument forms.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: Navigation/open/focus commands should carry or resolve into canonical route payload and retire generic page string routing where non-canonical.

verification_rules.summary: Reconciliation readiness requires canonical decisions for requested account, operational identity, trust vocabulary, route payload ownership, and project attention ownership.
verification_rules.raw_excerpt: Safe reconciliation requires canonical owners for requested concrete account, execution role disclosure, route payload schema, and project summary/attention projection.

verification_rules.summary: Readiness remains active until missing canonical event families and unresolved ownership seams are closed in SSOT docs.
verification_rules.raw_excerpt: If a seam still requires inventing a canonical event or record family, it is not yet reconciliation-ready.

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Projectors must derive summary state from canonical owners and must not invent blocked states unsupported by source objects.

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Missing canonical owner docs or event families indicate work is not reconciliation-ready and requires upstream ownership before downstream updates.
